**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Corio is the licensee/customer here, so I checked every place a Customer-payable liquidated amount would typically hide:

- **§4 Fees** — license, maintenance, tax and audit provisions only; the audit true-up (§4.4) is reciprocal shortfall/refund plus audit-cost reimbursement at a 5% underpayment threshold, which is a cost-recovery mechanic rather than a penalty.
- **§11 Term and Termination** — breach termination on 30 days' cure and non-renewal on 30 days' notice, with no early-termination fee, minimum-term make-whole, or acceleration of remaining fees. Surviving payment obligations attach only to Customers Corio chooses to keep supporting.
- **§9 Limitation of Liability** — mutual 12-month fee cap and consequential damages waiver; no stipulated-damages carve-out.
- **Exhibit B Pricing / Revenue Sharing / Payment Terms** — usage-based revenue share and net-30 terms; no late-payment interest, no minimum revenue commitment, no forfeiture language.

Amounts running toward us are unaffected and remain acceptable under the rule: Commerce One's MarketSite transaction revenue share, and our refund rights for prepaid fees on acceptance-test failure (§3) and uncorrected warranty breach (§7). The revenue share we pay Commerce One is consideration for usage, not a liquidated damage.

No deviation, so neither the fallback (3-month cap on any early-termination fee) nor any edit is needed on this rule.
